interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into pre-World War II economic intelligence, capital flight, and the financial maneuvers of Japanese institutions in the Territory of Hawaii and the continental United States nearly a year before the attack on Pearl Harbor. It documents FBI surveillance of Japanese financial operations and reveals proactive attempts by the Yokohama Specie Bank to repatriate or safeguard assets from prospective U.S. freezing orders, regulatory seizures, or receivership. Additionally, it illuminates how the Japanese diaspora in Hawaii utilized certificates of deposit to transfer private wealth under Japanese government control amid deteriorating U.S.-Japan relations.
overview: This file comprises a January 1941 communication from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., enclosing a confidential investigative memorandum concerning the activities of the Yokohama Specie Bank's branch in Honolulu, Hawaii. Based on informant reporting, the memorandum details inquiries by the Honolulu branch into the legality of transferring loan notes, collateral, and deposits to its parent institution in Yokohama, Japan, in an apparent effort to remove assets from the jurisdiction and control of the United States and the Territory of Hawaii. The report highlights that while such maneuvers might technically skirt violations of territorial banking law, they would prompt the territorial bank examiner to initiate receivership proceedings. It further reveals an unsuccessful attempt by branch officials to liquidate $2.5 million in pledged U.S. Government bonds, notes that identical legal strategies were circulated to branches in mainland U.S. cities, and describes efforts by Japanese residents in Hawaii to secure funds under Japanese government authority.

subfiles.summary: FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover transmits a confidential memorandum dated January 8, 1941, to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. The enclosed memorandum reports on investigative findings regarding the Yokohama Specie Bank in Yokohama, Japan, and its branch in Honolulu, Hawaii. The document includes Department of State filing and receipt markings from January 1941 under decimal classification 894.51611A/1.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. transmitting FBI memorandum

subfiles.about: Confidential FBI memorandum detailing legal queries and asset transfer maneuvers by the Yokohama Specie Bank branch in Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: A confidential informant reports that the Honolulu branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank sought legal opinions on moving promissory notes, collateral, and certificates of deposit to its parent bank in Japan, likely to evade territorial and U.S. control. Although the legal counsel concluded that transferring notes and collateral would not violate territorial banking laws, the territorial bank examiner would consider such actions unsound banking practice and seek a receivership. The memorandum also details the branch's denied request to liquidate $2.5 million in U.S. Government bonds held on deposit as security and shift the cash to local commercial banks for rapid withdrawal to Japan. Additionally, it notes that the legal advice was distributed to branches in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Portland, Seattle, and New York, and that local Japanese residents were depositing money in exchange for certificates of deposit payable in Japan.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Yokohama Specie Bank Operations in Honolulu
